26. And I have declared to them thy name, and will declare it. Christ discharged the office of Teacher, but, in order to make known the Father, he employed the secret revelation of the Spirit, and not the sound of his voice alone. He means, therefore, that he taught the apostles efficaciously. Besides, their faith being at that time very weak, he promises greater progress for the future, and thus prepares them to expect more abundant grace of the Holy Spirit. Though he speaks of the apostles, we ought to draw from this a general exhortation, to study to make constant progress, and not to think that we have run so well that we have not still a long journey before us, so long as we are surrounded by the flesh.
That the love with which thou hast loved me may be in them; that is, that thou mayest love them in me, or, that the love with which thou hast loved me may be extended to them; for, strictly speaking, the love with which God loves us is no other than that with which he loved his Son from the beginning, so as to render us also acceptable to him, and capablc of being loved in Christ. And, indeed, as was said a little before, so far as relates to us, apart from Christ, we are hated by God, and he only begins to love us, when we are united to the body of his beloved Son. It is an invaluable privilege of faith, that we know that Christ was loved by the Father on our account, that we might be made partakers of the same love, and might enjoy it for ever.
And I in them. This clause deserves our attention, for it teaches us that the only way in which we are included in that love which he mentions is, that Christ dwells in us; for, as the Father cannot look upon his Son without having likewise before his eyes the whole body of Christ, so, if we wish to be beheld in him, we must be actually his members.

John 18:1-6
1. When Jesus had spoken these words, he went out with his disciples over the brook Kedron, where was a garden, into which he entered, and his disciples. 2. And Judas also, who betrayed him, knew the place; for Jesus often resorted thither with his disciples. 3. Then Judas, having received a band of soldiers, and officers from the chief pricsts and Pharisees, came thither with lanterns, and torches, and weapons. 4. Now Jesus, knowing all the things which were coming upon him, went forward and said to them, Whom seek ye? 5. They answered him, Jesus of Nazareth. Jesus saith to them, It is I. And Judas also, who betrayed him, stood with them. 6. As soon therefore as he said to them, It is I, they went backward, and fell to the ground.

               <ns0:head>CHAP. XVII.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p>THese words spake Jesus; and lift up his eyes to heaven, and said <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">When our Lord had finished his Discourses, of which we have had a large account in <ns0:hi>Chap</ns0:hi> 14, 15, 16. he goes to prayer, as he taught us when we pray, to direct our pe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />titions to the father; so in this he setteth us an example, and before he speaketh, it is said <ns0:hi>he lifted up his eyes to Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven,</ns0:hi> as his Fathers Mansion-house; who tho he filleth Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven and Earth, yet doth in Heaven most manifest his glory; and therefore teaching us to pray, he commandeth us to say, <ns0:hi>Our Father which art in Heaven</ns0:hi>; not <ns0:hi>exclusively,</ns0:hi> as if God were not on Earth also: but <ns0:hi>eminently,</ns0:hi> as Heaven is the place where he most gloriously manifests himself. <ns0:hi>Lifting up of the eyes</ns0:hi> was an usual gesture in prayer, and but an in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dication of the Souls being lifted up, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 121.1. and 123.1. yet no necessary gesture: for we shall at another time find our Saviour <ns0:hi>falling upon his face</ns0:hi> when he prayed, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 26.39. <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 14.35: The lifting up of the Soul to God, wherein the main and Spiritual part of prayer lyes; doth not necessarily require the lifting up of the eyes. The <ns0:hi>Pub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lican</ns0:hi> cast down his eyes upon the Earth, in the sense of his unworthiness. Our Lord lifts up his eyes, and said, <ns0:hi>Father, the hour is come</ns0:hi>; that is, the hour of my Passion, the time wherein thou hast determined that I should die:</ns0:note>, Father <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 12.23. and 13.32.</ns0:note>, the hour is come <ns0:hi>b,</ns0:hi> glorifie thy Son, that thy Son also may glorifie thee <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">now make thy Son glorious, by raising me from the dead, by taking me up to Heaven; or by giving me assistance from thee to do the work which I have to do, to drink this bitter cup: that so I being risen again from the dead, and ascend<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing up to Heaven, may make thy name famous, by publish<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing thy <ns0:hi>Iustice, Goodness,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Truth,</ns0:hi> upon the Preaching of the Gospel to all Nations.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 11.27. and 28.18. Chap. 3.35. and 5.27. Heb. 2.8.</ns0:note> As thou hast given him power over all flesh <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">I see no reason for any to contend here, that by <ns0:hi>all flesh,</ns0:hi> the Elect onely who shall be eternally saved, are to be un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstood: Christs power undoubtedly extendeth further than to the Elect, (tho to them onely for Salvation) he hath a power over Reprobates and Unbelievers, to condemn them, as well as over his Elect to bring them to Eternal Life and Salvation. The former part of the Text speaketh of the more general Power and Authority, by which the Father had already made Christ Glorious; putting all things under his feet, and causing all knees to bow down unto him; which are other phrases by which the same things are expressed, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15.27. and <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 2.10. This gene<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral Power our Saviour executeth according to the Counsels of God, with respect to their faith or unbelief.</ns0:note>, that he should give eternal life to as many as thou hast given him <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">As to those given to Christ, that he should die in their stead, and with the price of his blood, purchase Eternal Life for them: Christ executeth his Power in giving them Eternal Life, under which notion, (as appeareth from many other Scrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tures) is comprehended, not the end onely, which is Eter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nal life and happiness, but all the necessary means in order to that end: from whence we are to observe, that <ns0:hi>Eternal Life</ns0:hi> is a free-gift, that the Son gives onely to such as the Father hath given him by his Eternal Counsels, so that all shall not be saved; for the term [as many as, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>] is plainly restrictive, and limits the gift to a certain number. And to examine our right to it, we need not ascend up into Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, to search the rolls of the Eternal Counsels; for all whom the Father hath given him, shall come unto him, and not onely receive him as their High Priest, but give up themselves to be ruled and guided by him, by the efficaci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous working of the Spirit of his grace; by such a receiving of Christ, and giving up of our selves to his Conduct and Government, we shall know whether we be of the number of those that are given to Christ; and till we find this, we have no reason to conclude it, but to fear and suspect the contrary.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 53.11. Jer. 9.24.</ns0:note> this is life eternal, that they might know thee the onely true God <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Those who deny the Divine Nature of Christ, think they have a mighty argument from this text; where Christ (as they say) speaking to his Father, calleth him the <ns0:hi>onely true God.</ns0:hi> But Divines answer, That the term <ns0:hi>onely</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>alone,</ns0:hi> is not to be applied to <ns0:hi>thee,</ns0:hi> but to the term <ns0:hi>God</ns0:hi>; and the sense this; To know <ns0:hi>thee, to be that God which is the one<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly true God</ns0:hi>; and this appeareth from 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 5.20. where Christ is said to be the <ns0:hi>true God,</ns0:hi> which he could not be if the Father were the onely true God, considered as another from the Son. The term <ns0:hi>onely</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>alone,</ns0:hi> is not exclusive of the other two persons in the Trinity, but onely of <ns0:hi>Idols,</ns0:hi> the Gods of the Heathen, which are no Gods; so 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 6.15, 16. and in many other Scriptures, so <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 11.27. where it is said, that <ns0:hi>none knoweth the Son, but the Father; neither knoweth any the Father, but the Son</ns0:hi>; where the negative doth not exclude the <ns0:hi>holy Spirit.</ns0:hi> Besides, the term <ns0:hi>alone,</ns0:hi> is in Scripture observed, not always to exclude all others as <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 6.47. Our Saviour saith, it is <ns0:hi>life eternal to know him who is the onely true God</ns0:hi>; that is, it is the way to Eternal Life, which is an ordinary figure used in holy Writ.</ns0:note>, and Jesus Christ whom thou hast sent <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">He adds, <ns0:hi>and Iesus Christ whom thou hast sent</ns0:hi>; by which he lets us know, that the Father cannot be sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vingly known, but in and by the Son. <ns0:hi>Knowing</ns0:hi> in this Verse, signifieth not the meer comprehending of God, and of Christ in mens Notions, but the receiving Christ, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieving in him, loving and obeying him, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:365" />4 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 13.32. and 14.13.</ns0:note> I have glorified thee on the earth <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">By Preaching the Gospel, by living up to the rule of thy Law, by the Miracles which I have wrought; God could not be glorified by Christ, by the addition of any thing to his Essential glory; onely by manifesting to the World his Fathers goodness, justice, mercy, truth, wisdom, and others of his Attributes.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 4.34. and 19.30.</ns0:note>: I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">One way by which he had glorified his Father, is exprest, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> by finishing the work which he had given him in Commission. But <ns0:hi>how could Christ say this, who had not yet died for the sins of men, which was the principal piece of his work</ns0:hi>? Ans. It was so nigh, that he speaks of it as already done; so <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 11. he saith, <ns0:hi>I am not in the world,</ns0:hi> because he was to be so little a time in the world. Again, he speaks of what he was fully resolved to do, as if it were already done.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">5 And now, O Father, glorifie thou me with thine own self, with the glory <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap 1.1, 2. and 1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.30. and 14.9.</ns0:note> which I had with thee before the world was <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Let the glory which as to my Divine Nature I had with thee before the foundation of the World, be commu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nicated also to my Human Nature, that my whole person may be made glorious; from hence is easily concluded a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst those which deny the Godhead of Christ, that Christ was glorified with his Father before the World was, which he could not have been, if he had not been Eternal God; he here begs of his Father, That that glory might shine upon his Person as Mediator.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 I have manifested thy Name unto the men <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Cha 6.37, 39. and 10.29.</ns0:note> which thou gavest me out of the world <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">There he openeth this former phrase, <ns0:hi>I have glorified thee upon earth</ns0:hi>; it was done by manifesting the Lords Name, proclaiming his goodness and mercy, publishing his Will, making famous all whereby God can be made known; this Christ did both by his words, and by his works.</ns0:note>: thine they were, and thou gavest them me; and they have kept thy word <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">This he had done (as he saith) to all those whom the Father had given him, whom the Father had given him by an Act of his Eternal Counsel; and by inclining their hearts to own and receive him when he came into the World; he tells his Father, that <ns0:hi>his they were.</ns0:hi> His chosen ones, and he had given them unto Christ, that he should redeem them with his blood, and take the care of their Salvation; and he saith, When I came and revealed thy Will unto them, they have not stubbornly and obstinately, as the generality of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> shut their eyes against the light, and rebelled against thy Will revealed; but they have heard, received, imbraced, and obeyed thy word.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 Now they have known that all things what<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />soever thou hast given me, are of thee <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">They have thus far made proficiency in the Doctrine which I have taught them; that tho the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> say, that <ns0:hi>I cast out Devils by Beelzebub the Prince of Devils,</ns0:hi> yet they believe, and are perswaded, that the Doctrine which I have taught them is from thee, and that it is by a Divine Power that I have wrought those miracles which I have wrought; and so I have manifested thy Name unto them, and they have received the manifestation and Revelation of thy Name un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 For I have given unto them the words <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 8.28. and 12.49. and 14.10.</ns0:note> which thou gavest me <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">Our Lord here doth both justifie himself, and commend these whom in this former part of his Prayer he is com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mending to his Father; he justifieth himself, that he had not delivered any thing to them, but what he had from his Father; thereby teaching all those who claim the Name of his Ministers what is their duty, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> to give to their hearers no word, but what God hath given them. If Christ confined his discourses to words which his Father had gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven him, certainly we ought to do so also. We are not to speak what we list, nor what men would have us; we are tied up to Gods word</ns0:note>; and they have received them <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">He commendeth these his Disci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ples, that they had received them, not onely the sound of them in their ears, not onely the Notion of them in their understandings, but they had imbraced and believed them;</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Chap. 16.27, 30.</ns0:note>, and have known surely that I came out from thee <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">and had from the force and authority of them, given cre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dit to him as the true Messias, who came out, and was sent from God. Tho they were not yet come up to a perfect faith in him as the Eternal Son of God; yet they believed him one that came from God, and was sent of God as the promised Messiah, which seemeth to have been that de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gree of faith which Christ most insisted upon as to his Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciples, until by his Resurrection from the dead, he decla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red himself to be the Son of God with Power; tho all a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />long this Gospel, his discourses, and the miracles which he wrought, had a particular tendency to prove himself one with the Father, and the Eternal Son of God; and the Disciples had some weak perswasion of this also.</ns0:note>, and they have believed that thou didst send me <ns0:hi>r.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 I pray for them, I pray not for the world <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">The World seemeth here to signifie all mankind, for whom Christ in this place doth not pray; tho some Inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pret it of <ns0:hi>Reprobates,</ns0:hi> others of <ns0:hi>Vnbelievers.</ns0:hi> Christ after<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ward prayeth for the World, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 20. that is, for such who, tho they at present were Unbelievers, yet should be brought to believe by the Apostles Ministry; but to teach us to di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stinguish in our prayer, our Saviour here distinguisheth, and prayeth for some things, for his chosen ones, which he doth not pray for on the behalf of others; these</ns0:note>: but for them which thou hast given me, for they are thine <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">he describeth to be such as his Father (whose they were) had given him, either by an Eternal donation, or by working faith in them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 And all mine are thine, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 16.15.</ns0:note> thine are mine: and I am glorified in thee <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">In the <ns0:hi>Greek,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Adjectives</ns0:hi> are of the <ns0:hi>neuter gender,</ns0:hi> so as the sense is not, All my friends, o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> all my Disciples are thine also; but, all my things are thine, and all thy things are mine; which is no more than he hath before often said. Christ and his Father have all things common, neither of them have any thing that is not the others. They are one, and they agree in one; they have the <ns0:hi>same Essence,</ns0:hi> the same <ns0:hi>Will,</ns0:hi> the same <ns0:hi>Attributes,</ns0:hi> the same <ns0:hi>Friends</ns0:hi>:</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">and I am (saith our Saviour) <ns0:hi>glorified,</ns0:hi> or made glorious <ns0:hi>in them,</ns0:hi> by their owning, receiving, and imbracing me, and accepting me as their Saviour. So as this Verse containeth two arguments more, inforcing his Petition on the behalf of his Elect. 1. His Fathers <ns0:hi>propriety in them,</ns0:hi> as well as his. 2. <ns0:hi>Their love to him,</ns0:hi> and the glory which redounded to him from their Faith and holiness.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 And now I am no more in the world <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">The term <ns0:hi>World</ns0:hi> in this Verse, signifies not the <ns0:hi>men of the World,</ns0:hi> nor any <ns0:hi>particular party</ns0:hi> of them, (as it often sig<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifieth) but <ns0:hi>the habitable part of the Earth.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour saith, he is no more in the World, because he was to conti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nue on the Earth but a very small time; but (saith he)</ns0:note>, but these are in the world <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">these my Disciples are like to abide in the World when I have left it; they will stand in need of this help, to be ar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />med against all the temptations they will meet with from the World. I am coming to thee,</ns0:note>, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">therefore I commend them to thee, beseeching thee, that thou through thy Power wouldest keep those, who in giving themselves up to me, have also given themselves up to thee; let their owning thy Name (which is as a strong tower, <ns0:hi>Prov.</ns0:hi> 18.10.) keep them from all the temptations and dangers, to which they will be exposed in the World, wherein they are to live and converse.</ns0:note>, those whom thou hast given me <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Ver. 21. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, that they may be one <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">Chap. 10.30.</ns0:note>, as we <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">That they may be one, one body, and in one Spirit, that they may own <ns0:hi>one Lord, one Faith, one Bap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tism, &c.</ns0:hi> that they may be <ns0:hi>one</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>love</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>affection,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>we are,</ns0:hi> in some proportion to that Union which is betwixt thee and me, tho not in an equality. This Prayer of our Saviours doth both oblige all those who in any sincerity own Christ, to study Union both in Opinion and Affection; and also give us ground of hopes, that there is a time coming, when there shall be greater measure of it than we have seen in those miserably divided times wherein we have lived, and do yet live.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 While I was with them in the world <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 6.39<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and 10.28. Heb. 13 5, 6.</ns0:note>, I kept them in thy Name <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Christ speaks here of himself as one who had already dyed, was Risen, and Ascended, tho none of all these things were past, because they were so suddenly to come to pass. I have (saith our Saviour) for all the time that I have abode in the World, and conversed with them, kept them <ns0:hi>in thy Name, i. e.</ns0:hi> in the steady owning and profession of thy truth; or (if we read it <ns0:hi>through thy Name</ns0:hi>) it signifieth through thy Power, and the influence of thy Grace.</ns0:note>: those that thou gavest me, I have kept <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">Chap. 18.9.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">I have not so kept all that came to hear me, but all those whom thou gavest me by the act of thy Eternal Counsel; or whom thou gavest me to be my Apostles:</ns0:note>, and none of them is lost <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Chap. 6.70. and 13.18<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note>, but the son of perdition <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">and none of them is proved an Apostate, but the <ns0:hi>Son of Perdition</ns0:hi>: none of them is lost whom thou gavest me by thy Eternal gift, none of them whom thou gavest me to be my Apostles, but one, who tho he was my <ns0:hi>Apostle,</ns0:hi> and in that sense given to me, yet was never given me by thy Eternal gift, as one to be by me Redeemed, and brought to Eternal life and Sal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vation; for he was a <ns0:hi>Son of Perdition</ns0:hi>: we have this term applyed to Antichrist, 2 <ns0:hi>Thes.</ns0:hi> 2.3. As the <ns0:hi>Son of Death,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 12.5. signifies one appointed to die, or that deser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />veth to die. And the <ns0:hi>child of Hell, Matth.</ns0:hi> 23.15. signifieth one who deserveth Hell. So the <ns0:hi>Son of Perdition</ns0:hi> may ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther signifie one destinated to Perdition, or one that walk<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth in the high and right road to Perdition, or rather both; one who being past over in Gods Eternal Counsels, as to such as shall be saved; hath by his own wilful Apostacy brought himself to <ns0:hi>Eternal Perdition,</ns0:hi> or into such a guilt as I know thou wilt destroy him.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>09.81</ns0:note>: that the scripture might be fulfilled <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">And by this the holy Scripture is fulfilled. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 109.1, 8. for that is the portion of Scripture here intended, as is apparent from <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.20. where the Apostle applyeth that text to <ns0:hi>Iudas,</ns0:hi> who is here spoken of. Other Scriptures also were thus fulfilled, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 41.9. compared with <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 13.18.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:366" />13 And now I come to thee <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">He speaketh still in the present tense. These words were not fulfilled six weeks after this; for <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 1.3. he conversed with his Disciples forty days after his Resurrection; but Christ was now shortly coming, therefore he saith I come.</ns0:note>, and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">And saith he, while I am in the World, I <ns0:hi>speak these things</ns0:hi>; I put up this prayer, that the joy of my peo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple may not be diminished by my going from them, but that when they can no longer (as hitherto) rejoice in my bodily presence with them, they may yet rejoyce, that I am ascended to my Father, that they stand commended to the care of thee my Father, by this my last Pray<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 I have given them thy word <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">I take more to be understood here, by Christs giving his word unto his Disciples, than his Preaching the Gospel in their ears; otherwise Christ had no more given these his Disciples his word, than he had given it to many thou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sands of others who were yet in the World, and whom the World hated not. The sense therefore is, I have not onely Preached thy word in their ears, but I have opened their hearts to receive, and believe it, and bowed their wills to a complian<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> with it; so a<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> the word dwelleth in their hearts, is ingraffed in them, and they are turned into the likeness of it. And here it is observable, That when any Soul is given to Christ by his Father, Christ will most certainly first or last give unto that Soul his word in that sense; that is, so as it shall receive, believe it, and be turned into the likeness of it.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 15 18, 19.</ns0:note> the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">And for this the World hath hated them, for thy word hath made them to be of another Spirit, from carnal, loose, and Worldly men; they have other affections, other inclinations, other designs and studies; they are not of the World</ns0:note>, even as I am not of the world <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">in that respect, as I am not of the World: tho in other respects not so; for Christ as to his Original, was not of the World, which they were, <ns0:hi>of the Earth, Earthly.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Mat. 6.13. 1 John 5.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>18.</ns0:note> keep them from the evil <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Christ doth not pray that his Father would take up his Saints out of this sinful and troublesome World into Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, because he knew that they were to be of use to him for a time in the World; but he prays that the Lord would keep them from the evil one (so some would have it transla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted) or from the <ns0:hi>evil thing</ns0:hi>; by which we must not under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand what is penally and afflictively evil, but onely what is sinfully evil: and by his example he hath directed us how we ought to pray; not for death, nor absolutely for a deli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verance from the evils; and miseries of this life, but that we may be delivered from those temptations to sin, to which a multitude of sharp tryals and afflictions will expose even the best of men.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">This is the same thing which he had said before, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 14. which he again repeateth, either to fix it in their me<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mories, that they calling it to their minds, might direct their lives accordingly, or be thereby fortified against the hatred and malice of the World; for which purpose he told them so before, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 15.19. and again in this <ns0:hi>Chapter, ver.</ns0:hi> 14. (see the notes on Verse 14.)</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 Sanctifie them through thy truth <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">It is doubted amongst Interpreters, whether <ns0:hi>Sancti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fying</ns0:hi> in this place, signifieth the consecrating, deputing, or setting the Apostles apart, and preparing them for the work of the Ministry in which they were to be imployed; as the word signifies, <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 1.15. or the strengthning and confirm<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing their Habits of Grace, so as they might be able to en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />counter the temptations they should meet with from the hatred or opposition of the World; or 3. the perfecting of them in Holiness. Mr. <ns0:hi>Calvin</ns0:hi> saith, our Saviour here Prayeth, that God would appropriate them unto himself:</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 8.46.</ns0:note>: thy word is truth <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">and he sheweth how this is done, <ns0:hi>through, or in the truth</ns0:hi>; that is, (some say) <ns0:hi>through thy truth</ns0:hi> ingraven, and im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />printed upon their hearts by thine Holy Spirit, which was promised to <ns0:hi>lead</ns0:hi> and to guide them into all truth, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 16.13. (say others) <ns0:hi>through thy Spirit,</ns0:hi> which indeed is the Sanctifier; and we have met with twice, called, <ns0:hi>The Spirit of truth, Chap.</ns0:hi> 14.17. Some say, <ns0:hi>Sanctifie them in thy truth,</ns0:hi> is no more than Sanctifie them truly, in opposition to that legal Sanctification of Priests, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> of which we read in the Books of <ns0:hi>Exodus</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Leviticus.</ns0:hi> Others would have it <ns0:hi>to thy truth</ns0:hi>; that is, to the Preaching of thy Gospel. But our Translation seems to come nearest the meaning, <ns0:hi>through thy truth,</ns0:hi> that is, through the knowledge of thy truth; as the Gentiles are said to have had their hearts pu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rified by faith, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 15.9.</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">He opens what he meant by truth, adding, <ns0:hi>thy word is truth</ns0:hi>; that is, thy word and Gospel, which I have Preached to them, is <ns0:hi>truth</ns0:hi>; (the ab<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stract, as some think, for the concrete) that is, it is most true; it is not like the Doctrine of false Prophets, nor like the Doctrine of the <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> which is partly true, partly false; but it is truth it self: and tho indeed it is the <ns0:hi>blood of Christ</ns0:hi> which cleanseth and purifieth the heart, yet this is applyed to the conscience by the Spirit, which is the San<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctifier, in and through the word of God Preached and ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plyed to the Soul.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap, 20.21.</ns0:note> As thou hast sent me into the world: even so have I also sent them into the world <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">That is, My Father! they have not thrust themselves into their imployment, they have not run without sending; for as I am thine Apostle, as I was sent by thee, so I have sent them. The Apostles indeed were not sent for the same end in all things that Christ was sent; who was sent to pur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chase Salvation for men, as well as to Preach the Gospel: but they were sent in part for the same work for which Christ was sent, and they were sent by him who had au<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thority to send them; and as it is but reasonable for Princes to protect those whom themselves send upon their Embas<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sies; so it was but reasonable that God should defend and protect those whom his Son had sent out as his Embassa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dors.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 1.2, 30. 1 Thes. 4.7.</ns0:note> for their sakes I sanctifie my self <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">I <ns0:hi>Sanctifie my self,</ns0:hi> here, is no more than I set my self apart, as a Sacrifice acceptable, and well-pleasing in the sight of God: and indeed sanctifying in the ancient notion of it under the Law, did ordinarily signifie the setting of persons and things apart to the special Service of God, which was done <ns0:hi>legally,</ns0:hi> by certain ritual performances and cere<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />monies, and is still done <ns0:hi>inwardly</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Spiritually</ns0:hi> by Rege<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neration, and renewing of the hearts of men and women by the efficacious working of the Holy Ghost. Christ saith, that for his Disciples <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ake he sanctified himself, being both the <ns0:hi>Priest</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Sacrifice.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, that they also might be sanctified <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>truly Sanctified.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> through the truth <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Christ set apart himself as a <ns0:hi>Sacrifice</ns0:hi> for his people, <ns0:hi>that they might be sanctified,</ns0:hi> not onely our Eternal life and Happiness, but all the means to it fell within the Counsel of God; hence we are said to be chosen of Christ, <ns0:hi>that we should be holy, and without blame before him in love</ns0:hi>; and within the <ns0:hi>purchase of Christ</ns0:hi>; hence the Apostle saith, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 5 25. <ns0:hi>That he gave himself for his Church, that he might sanctifie and cleanse it with the wash<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of water</ns0:hi>: and our Saviour here saith, that he set apart himself for a Sacrifice for our sins, that his people might be <ns0:hi>Sanctified</ns0:hi> through the truth; that is, by receiving the truth, not in their ears onely, but in their hearts, in the love of it, and bringing forth the fruits of it in all Holiness of life and conversation.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 Neither pray I for these alone: but for them also which shall believe on me through their word <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Two things are evident from this Verse. 1. That Christ did not pray for any Reprobates, not for any that were and should die unbelievers; he prayed before for those who actually did believe; he prayeth here <ns0:hi>for them that should believe</ns0:hi>; but we never read that he prayed for any others: Now whether he laid down his life for those for whom he would not pray, lyeth upon them to consider, who are so confident, that he died for all and every man. 2. That by persons <ns0:hi>given to Christ,</ns0:hi> cannot be understood believers as such; for Christ here prayeth for those that were no actual believers, but should believe. 3. That <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>aith cometh by hearing; Christ here prayeth for those that should believe through <ns0:hi>their word,</ns0:hi> that is, the Apostles Preaching the Gospel.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:366" />21 <ns0:note place="margin">Ver. 11.22, 23. Ga<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. 3.28.</ns0:note> That they all may be one, as <ns0:note place="margin">Chap 10.38. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>nd 14.11.</ns0:note> thou, Father, <ns0:hi>art</ns0:hi> in me, and <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap> in thee <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Our Saviour here prayeth on the behalf of such as should believe on him, That they might <ns0:hi>be one</ns0:hi> in faith, and one in brotherly love; who so considereth this as a piece of Christs prayer for Believers, and that St. <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> hardly wrote one Epistle to the Primitive Apostolical Churches, in which he did not press this by most potent Arguments, cannot but nourish some hopes, (how improbable soever it appears at present) that all the sincere Disciples of Christ, shall one day arrive at the keeping of the Unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace; and likewise look upon themselves in point of duty, obliged to indeavour it. To which pitch of perfecti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on possibly <ns0:hi>Christians</ns0:hi> might soon arrive, if Superiors would after the Example of the Apostle, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 15.28. lay upon their Inferiors no more than <ns0:hi>necessary things</ns0:hi>; and equals would learn to contend for truth in <ns0:hi>love,</ns0:hi> and to walk with their brethren so far as they have attained; and as to other things, <ns0:hi>to forbear one another in love</ns0:hi>; and wherein any of their brethren are otherwise minded, then they are to wait till God shall reveal it to them, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 3.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note>; that they also may be one in us <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">But this is not all the Union which Christ prayeth for; he also prayeth that they might be one in the Father and the Son; that is, that they might believe; for Faith is that Grace by which we are united to, and made one with God and Christ; tho others interpret it of obedience, or such things wherein God the Father and Christ are one, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> For, altho so many as are ordained to Life shall believe, yet that they might believe, is matter of Prayer:</ns0:note>: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">this our Saviour prayeth for, for the further glory of God, which is that which he mean<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth by the Worlds believing that God had sent him; there being no greater evidence that Christ is the true <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> than the general acceptance of the Doctrine of the Gospel, which he brought throughout the World; for who can imagine, that a new Doctrine brought into the World by one of no greater reputation than Christ had in the World<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and propagated by persons of no greater quality than the Apostles were, should obtain in the greatest part of the World, if he that first introduced it, had not been first sent by God into the World, and the Apostles had not been ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />traordinarily influenced and assisted by God as to the pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pagation of it, after Christ was Ascended into Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven?</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 And the glory which thou hast given me, I have given them <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">By glory here, some understand the Heavenly glo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry; but then they must understand the <ns0:hi>Oneness</ns0:hi> mentioned in the latter part of the Verse, of the Union which the Saints shall have with Christ and his Father in glory, in another World. Others understand the Divine Nature, of which the Apostle, 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 1.4. saith; believers are made partakers; this seemeth to come nearer for the more men and women are made partakers of that, the more they will study the <ns0:hi>unity of the Spirit.</ns0:hi> Others understand <ns0:hi>the power of working Miracles,</ns0:hi> by which Christ is said to have manifested his glo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 2.11. and the the effect of this Power, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 11.40. is called <ns0:hi>the glory of God.</ns0:hi> Others understand <ns0:hi>the preach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of the Gospel,</ns0:hi> in which <ns0:hi>the ministration of the Spirit is glorious,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 3.8, and the faithful Ministers of the Gospel are called <ns0:hi>the glory of Christ.</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 8.23.</ns0:note>: that they may be one, even as we are one <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">Our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour either again repeats his prayer, that they might be one; or else declareth that he had communicated his power, his glory to them, that they might be one, as he and his Fa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther are one.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 I in them <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">I <ns0:hi>in them,</ns0:hi> not onely as my Divine Nature is united <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>o their fles<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, but as I have made them partakers of my Spi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rit, and of the Divine Nature; as I have loved them with a special and peculiar love, and am the <ns0:hi>head,</ns0:hi> they the <ns0:hi>Mem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bers</ns0:hi>; I the <ns0:hi>Vine,</ns0:hi> they the <ns0:hi>Branches</ns0:hi>:</ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">that they may be made perfect in one, (the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> is, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> into one) In <ns0:hi>one body,</ns0:hi> whereof Christ is the Head; which body is the Church, keeping an unity <ns0:hi>of faith</ns0:hi>; All believing the same things in matter of faith, and those things no other than what thou hast revealed, and I have revealed as from thee.</ns0:note>, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">and <ns0:hi>thou in me, the fulness of the Godhead dwelling in me bodily</ns0:hi>; I being <ns0:hi>the brightness of thy glory, the express image of thy Person.</ns0:hi> Thou also doing whatsoever I do, and accepting and ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />proving of it, as <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 14.10.</ns0:note>, and that the world may know that thou hast sent me, and hast loved them, as thou hast loved me <ns0:hi>z.</ns0:hi>
                  <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">This, O Father! will be a great evidence, b<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>

               <ns0:p n="24">24 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap 12.26.</ns0:note> Father, I will that they also whom thou hast given me, be with me where I am <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Here our Saviour willeth his Disciples Eternal Life or rather prayeth to his Father, that he would preserve his Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciples unto, and at last bestow upon them Eternal Life and Salvation; so as the phrase, <ns0:hi>whom thou hast given me,</ns0:hi> is not to be restrained to the Apostles, but to be extended to all those who belonging to the election of Grace, shall hereaf<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter be made heirs of glory, and have everl<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
